findings.conclusion: One complete native trajectory per actor training row, both in official LOOP and the frozen thin bridge. The 3358 completion response records are a separate retained table and do not replace the 216-row trajectory batch.

32 global trajectories per minibatch; actor rollout.n default 1 is separate from environment rollout.n 6; DP2 normalizes to local mini16. For the stated 216 trajectory collection, original adjust_batch divisor8 causes no copy; 108 rows per rank split as 6x16+12. Two epochs gives expected14 optimizer steps per rank, not ceil(3358/32)*2.

findings.conclusion: LOOP _get_tensors takes the complete PolicyTokenInfo history capped by learning_max_seq_len, and _loss computes log-probs across this history once. The bridge takes the identical native token artifact and prefix cap, with output mask copied from is_output; one-token prompt leaves later observations as masked context. VERL log-prob uses that same full trajectory table, microbatched at4.

The sample unit matches, but LOOP and VERL token weights are not numerically identical: LOOP averages the surrogate over each trajectory output-token vector before accumulating trajectory losses; current upstream VERL uses masked token-mean over each B4 microbatch then divides by gradient_accumulation4. Relative per-token weight is inverse of that trajectory output count in LOOP, versus inverse of the B4 output-token total in VERL. PLAN explicitly retains VERL owner PPO and its approved whole-batch masked_whiten; this difference does not show response expansion or authorize importing LOOP trainer logic.

Original LOOP performs RLOO-based absolute-advantage trajectory filtering before optimizer splitting, can keep fewer than the collected216, and reshuffles per epoch. It is not valid to claim exact original-LOOP full-run optimizer-count equivalence from collection size alone; no filter substitution is proposed.
